title: Sparkline SDK environment spin-up + auth & Optimize walkthrough
summary: Intro + live SDK pairing (Python/TS) to get a sandbox app calling Redwood API, cover auth patterns (API key vs SSO/OIDC for Dedicated), environment variables, CI secrets, brief Optimize recommendations (batching/caching), and next steps to run a 1-week pilot and a small latency benchmark.
topics: Auth: API keys, SSO/OIDC, KMS for Private
Environment setup: sandbox, CI secrets, dotenv
Console walkthrough: routes, logs, token cost breakdown
Redwood Optimize suggestions: batching, cache, quantization

Samir Patel: Export small sample benchmark script (python + ts) and example payloads — due 2025-12-15
Jordan Lee: Provision test dataset and send sample prompts — due 2025-12-14
Maya Ortiz: Confirm SOC2 questions list and provide point of contact for security review — due 2025-12-18

Customer to run 3x latency tests and share results

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-12-11
Start time: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Avery Cole (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Sparkline Dev Lead), Priya Raman (Sparkline Infra), Ethan Green (Sparkline Product), Maya Ortiz (Sparkline Security)
---
[00:00] Avery Cole: Hey everyone, thanks for coming on. I'm Avery, I'm the AE working with Sparkline. Quick high level — Samir and I will pair through a very small SDK spin-up, auth patterns, and then Samir will show a few Optimize recommendations.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Hi, thanks — excited. We're focused on a quick dev path to integrate embeddings and a chat summarizer, mostly Python backend and TS frontend.
[00:20] Priya Raman: We have a VPC requirement for sensitive data and we need to understand Dedicated vs Private. Also lifecycle for keys — we use HashiCorp.
[00:30] Samir Patel: Great, we'll cover both. Quick note: some of the names in automatic transcripts might look off, bear with me. We'll start with a live demo in the Python SDK then mirror it in TypeScript.
[00:45] Ethan Green: Also curious about cost tradeoffs — latency vs cost with batching.
[00:50] Avery Cole: Yep we'll touch Optimize there. Ok Samir, take it away.
[01:00] Samir Patel: Alright I'm sharing my screen — starting in a minimal venv. First step: pip install redwood-sdk (note: package naming may vary in early access).
[01:15] Jordan Lee: Do you support both open-source models and Redwood-verified variants?
[01:20] Samir Patel: Yes, the catalog shows both. For quickstart we pick a small gpt-ish open model for lower token costs.
[01:30] Samir Patel: Code snippet: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_KEY')) — small pause, this is the API key flow for hosted.
[01:45] Priya Raman: For Private, do we still use an API key or are we doing OIDC?
[01:50] Samir Patel: Good Q. For Private we recommend OIDC/SSO tied to your IdP and short-lived certs; for Dedicated we can do API keys backed by KMS and rotate with your HashiCorp Vault — there are examples in the runbook.
[02:05] Jordan Lee: Any gotchas with dotenv and CI?
[02:10] Samir Patel: Use env vars in CI, don't check into repo. We showed a small .env example and a GitHub Actions snippet that pulls the secret from your secrets store.
[02:22] [crosstalk] Maya Ortiz: And audit logs?
[02:24] Avery Cole: Console provides token-level logs and audit trails; in Private you can push logs to your SIEM via our logging stream.
[02:35] Samir Patel: Switching to the TS side — npx create-redwood-app (toy example). Import from '@redwood/sdk' and new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY }).
[02:50] Jordan Lee: How do we handle user-to-user redaction or PII?
[02:55] Samir Patel: We have built-in redaction hooks and also recommend prefix/KV cache avoidance for sensitive prefixes; plus you can route sensitive calls to Private deployment with no shared telemetry.
[03:10] Samir Patel: Live test — simple chat completion, then an embeddings call for search. Sending small payload (shows token counts).
[03:30] Samir Patel: Note, streaming is enabled by default for low-latency UI; here's how to consume an SSE stream in TS.
[03:50] Ethan Green: That streaming example — will it re-auth or refresh tokens?
[03:55] Samir Patel: For long-lived streams, we recommend short-lived session tokens that you refresh via your backend. We'll share code.
[04:10] Jordan Lee: Ok. On to Optimize — what quick wins should we try in the first sprint?
[04:15] Samir Patel: Three quick levers: 1) batching for fanout embedding jobs, 2) prefix/KV caching for repeat prompts in chat summarization, 3) model quantization profile for throughput on Dedicated GPUs. We'll demo a small batching tweak.
[04:35] Samir Patel: Example: batch size 16 for embeddings reduces per-unit cost but watch tail latency. Our Console has recommended batch curves per model.
[04:50] Priya Raman: For our SLAs we care about p95. How does Redwood surface that?
[04:55] Avery Cole: Console shows per-route p50/p95/p99, token breakdown and cost — you can set alerts on regressions.
[05:10] Samir Patel: Quick demo of the Console: route list, route settings, rollout policy (canary percent), fallback to smaller model when overloaded.
[05:30] Jordan Lee: Any latency numbers from prior customers on similar workloads?
[05:35] Samir Patel: We published a benchmark for a 1k token chat scenario: hosted p95 ~420ms, Dedicated with optimized kernels can hit ~160ms on A100-ish hardware with quantization. These are illustrative.
[05:55] Maya Ortiz: Security: do you integrate with our KMS for key rotation when using Private?
[06:00] Samir Patel: Yes, we support external KMS/HSM — keys never leave your control. We'll add a short architecture diagram to the runbook.
[06:15] Jordan Lee: How do we measure quality regressions when changing model or quantization?
[06:20] Samir Patel: Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring to prompt sets and evals — you can run A/B and we surface delta in embeddings similarity or hallucination metrics. We can onboard a few of your prompt tests.
[06:40] [screen share pause — Samir opens an example repo]
[07:00] Samir Patel: Repo layout: examples/python/quickstart.py and examples/ts/frontend.tsx. Let's run the python example live — note the sandbox key.
[07:15] [typing]
[07:35] quickstart.py output: "Request sent — 0.3s, tokens: 68" (automated transcript shows raw console text).
[07:45] Jordan Lee: That latency looks good for dev. For prod we'd want to test under load.
[07:50] Samir Patel: Absolutely — we'll hand a small load test script.
[08:05] Priya Raman: On infra: does Redwood push a connector into our VPC or do we open egress only?
[08:12] Samir Patel: For Hosted it's outbound only. For Dedicated in VPC mode, we deploy within your VPC or run a peered network — different options depending on security. Private is fully customer-managed.
[08:25] Maya Ortiz: Can you sign a DPA and provide SOC2 reports?
[08:30] Avery Cole: Yes, standard DPA and SOC2 Type II available — we'll send the packet.
[08:38] Ethan Green: Are there retention controls for logs and request data?
[08:42] Samir Patel: Retention configurable per-org; you can set zero retention for sensitive orgs in Private.
[08:55] Jordan Lee: Ok let's talk pilot scope. We want embeddings for search of product docs and a chat summarizer on user support transcripts. Goal: 2-week pilot.
[09:05] Avery Cole: Suggested pilot: 1) provision sandbox, 2) integrate backend embeddings endpoints, 3) run a 3-day throughput/latency test and 4) review Optimize recommendations. We can compress to 1 week if you have engineers ready.
[09:20] Jordan Lee: We do; we'll aim for the one-week fast path.
[09:24] Samir Patel: I'll note a quick checklist in the runbook: environment vars, secrets, sample load test, CI snippet, streaming example, and a small TS widget demo.
[09:40] [laughter] Priya Raman: Please make the CI snippet copy-paste friendly.
[09:42] Samir Patel: Will do.
[09:48] Maya Ortiz: A couple of deeper security questions: encryption at rest for the KV cache and whether tokens are masked in logs.
[09:55] Samir Patel: KV cache can be encrypted with your KMS; token masking is applied but we'll need to review a specific retention policy. We'll have security docs.
[10:10] Jordan Lee: Any examples of using HashiCorp Vault for rotation?
[10:15] Samir Patel: Yes, we have a short script that rotates API keys via Vault and hits Redwood's rotation endpoint. Samir to share.
[10:25] Avery Cole: Ok quick recap before we wrap.
[10:28] Avery Cole: Actions — Avery will send sandbox invite + runbook; Samir sends example scripts and benchmark harness; Jordan will provision sample data; Maya will send security contact and confirm SOC2 items. Any other blockers?
[10:40] Ethan Green: Pricing — can you send an estimate for hosted vs Dedicated for our expected volume?
[10:45] Avery Cole: Yes I'll include a starter estimate in the follow-up email.
[10:52] Jordan Lee: Final question — is there an offline on-prem package for air-gapped?
[10:56] Samir Patel: Yes we have an on-prem package as part of Private, though the install can take more ops time. We'll discuss scope if you go that route.
[11:10] Avery Cole: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with materials and schedule the SE deep dive Thursday.
[11:20] Jordan Lee: Thanks, talk soon.
---
Notes: transcript contains minor transcription errors (package names and exact CLI verbs), some speaker overlaps. The live repo used a temporary sandbox key which was not shared in recording.
